<!--
Feature requests are fine, with a few realities up front:

- The maintenance bar is high. Hoptrail aims to do one thing well
  (continuous path probing with per-hop attribution); the maintainer
  is conservative about adding more, especially for use cases not
  personally exercised.
- There is no public roadmap beyond the milestones in the README, and
  no committed delivery dates. If a request lands in the maintainer's
  own backlog, you may see it in a future release. If it doesn't, it
  doesn't.
- A "no" isn't an indictment of the idea. It usually means the idea is
  good but not aligned with where the codebase is going. That's exactly
  the case where forking makes sense — the MIT license has you covered.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for the longer version.
-->

## What you'd like hoptrail to do

<!-- A clear description of the feature or change you're suggesting. -->

## Why it matters to you

<!--
Concrete use case from your own network setup, ideally. The "I want it
for myself" filter applies in reverse here: when a feature is something
the suggester actually uses, the design discussion is much sharper
than abstract framing.
-->

## How it might fit (optional)

<!-- Where in the existing UI, daemon, or architecture you imagine this living. Skip if you don't have an opinion. -->

## What you've already tried (optional)

<!--
If you've worked around the absence of this feature with a config
tweak, an external script, another network tool, or something on the
network side, a quick note about that helps calibrate how much friction
the gap is causing.
-->
